\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ویران} \fa{شدن} (virân shodan)}{ویران شدن (virân shodan)}]{\fa{ویران} \fa{شدن} (virân shodan) — to be destroyed, to be ruined}

\label{lesson:FA-C331-viran-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a warning, then the Persian for to warn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ویران} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{ویران} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{virân shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be destroyed, to be ruined\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{زلزله} \fa{صدها} \fa{خانه} \fa{ویران} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar zelzele sad-hâ khâne virân shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Hundreds of houses were destroyed in the earthquake.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{virân mishavad}. \emph{Virân} \textquotedblleft{}ruined\textquotedblright{} is also an adjective.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{virân} \textquotedblleft{}desolate, ruined\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word that EtymDB lists without a parent; \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{virân shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{virân shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{virân shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a warning, then the Persian for to warn, then say \emph{virân shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{ویران} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be destroyed, to be ruined\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن} (foru rikhtan)}{فرو ریختن (foru rikhtan)}]{\fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن} (foru rikhtan) — to collapse, to cave in}

\label{lesson:FA-C331-foru-rikhtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to warn, then the Persian for to be destroyed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن}}
\textbf{\fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن}} (\emph{foru rikhtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to collapse, to cave in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سقف} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{قدیمی} \fa{فرو} \fa{ریخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Saqf-e madrese-ye qadimi foru rikht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The roof of the old school collapsed.
\end{quote}

\emph{foru} \textquotedblleft{}down\textquotedblright{} + \emph{rikhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to pour\textquotedblright{}. Present stem \emph{riz-}: \emph{foru mirizad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{foru} \textquotedblleft{}down\textquotedblright{} is native Persian, and \emph{rikhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to pour\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB): to pour down.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{foru rikhtan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{foru rikhtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{foru rikhtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to warn, then the Persian for to be destroyed, then say \emph{foru rikhtan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To collapse, to cave in\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آوار} (âvâr)}{آوار (âvâr)}]{\fa{آوار} (âvâr) — rubble, debris}

\label{lesson:FA-C331-avar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be destroyed, then the Persian for to collapse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آوار}}
\textbf{\fa{آوار}} (\emph{âvâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}rubble, debris\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{امدادگرها} \fa{دو} \fa{نفر} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{زیر} \fa{آوار} \fa{بیرون} \fa{آوردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Emdâdgar-hâ do nafar râ az zir-e âvâr birun âvardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rescue workers pulled two people out from under the rubble.
\end{quote}

\emph{Zir-e âvâr} \textquotedblleft{}under the rubble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âvâr} \textquotedblleft{}rubble\textquotedblright{} is a Persian word whose origin is not settled; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âvâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be destroyed, then the Persian for to collapse, then say \emph{âvâr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تخلیه} \fa{کردن} (takhliye kardan)}{تخلیه کردن (takhliye kardan)}]{\fa{تخلیه} \fa{کردن} (takhliye kardan) — to evacuate, to empty}

\label{lesson:FA-C331-takhliye-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to collapse, then the Persian for rubble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تخلیه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تخلیه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{takhliye kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to evacuate, to empty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{ساختمان} \fa{را} \fa{تخلیه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis sâkhtemân râ takhliye kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police evacuated the building.
\end{quote}

Also \textquotedblleft{}to empty, to unload\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{takhliye mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{takhliye} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{takhliya} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}an emptying, a clearing\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{takhliye kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to collapse, then the Persian for rubble, then say \emph{takhliye kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پناه} \fa{بردن} (panâh bordan)}{پناه بردن (panâh bordan)}]{\fa{پناه} \fa{بردن} (panâh bordan) — to take shelter, to take refuge}

\label{lesson:FA-C331-panah-bordan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for rubble, then the Persian for to evacuate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پناه} \fa{بردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پناه} \fa{بردن}} (\emph{panâh bordan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to take shelter, to take refuge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مردم} \fa{از} \fa{باران} \fa{به} \fa{زیر} \fa{پل} \fa{پناه} \fa{بردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mardom az bârân be zir-e pol panâh bordand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People took shelter from the rain under the bridge.
\end{quote}

\emph{panâh} \textquotedblleft{}refuge\textquotedblright{} + \emph{bordan} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}. Present stem \emph{bar-}: \emph{panâh mibarad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{panâh} \textquotedblleft{}refuge\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{panāh}, \textquotedblleft{}protector, refuge\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{bordan} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{panâh bordan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{panâh bordan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for rubble, then the Persian for to evacuate, then say \emph{panâh bordan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 324–331 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R331-review-324-331}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for a mishap and a disaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a mishap, a disaster, to crash, to collide, to overturn
  \item to fall over, to get twisted, to get hurt, to be harmed, a fracture
  \item injured, a wound, bleeding, to faint, to come round
  \item a rescue worker, the emergency services, a siren, to survive, a lifeguard
  \item a fire, to catch fire, a flame, smoke, a spark
  \item an explosion, to explode, to burst, to leak, ash
  \item a storm, to drown, to crash down, a warning, to warn
  \item to be destroyed, to collapse, rubble, to evacuate, to take shelter
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A mishap? (\textbf{\fa{حادثه}}.) A disaster? (\textbf{\fa{سانحه}}.) To crash? (\textbf{\fa{تصادف} \fa{کردن}}.) To collide? (\textbf{\fa{برخورد} \fa{کردن}}.) To overturn? (\textbf{\fa{واژگون} \fa{شدن}}.) To fall over? (\textbf{\fa{زمین} \fa{خوردن}}.) To get twisted? (\textbf{\fa{پیچ} \fa{خوردن}}.) To get hurt? (\textbf{\fa{آسیب} \fa{دیدن}}.) To be harmed? (\textbf{\fa{صدمه} \fa{دیدن}}.) A fracture? (\textbf{\fa{شکستگی}}.) Injured? (\textbf{\fa{مصدوم}}.) A wound? (\textbf{\fa{جراحت}}.) Bleeding? (\textbf{\fa{خونریزی}}.) To faint? (\textbf{\fa{بیهوش} \fa{شدن}}.) To come round? (\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{هوش} \fa{آمدن}}.) A rescue worker? (\textbf{\fa{امدادگر}}.) The emergency services? (\textbf{\fa{اورژانس}}.) A siren? (\textbf{\fa{آژیر}}.) To survive? (\textbf{\fa{زنده} \fa{ماندن}}.) A lifeguard? (\textbf{\fa{غریق} \fa{نجات}}.) A fire? (\textbf{\fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی}}.) To catch fire? (\textbf{\fa{آتش} \fa{گرفتن}}.) A flame? (\textbf{\fa{شعله}}.) Smoke? (\textbf{\fa{دود}}.) A spark? (\textbf{\fa{جرقه}}.) An explosion? (\textbf{\fa{انفجار}}.) To explode? (\textbf{\fa{منفجر} \fa{شدن}}.) To burst? (\textbf{\fa{ترکیدن}}.) To leak? (\textbf{\fa{نشت} \fa{کردن}}.) Ash? (\textbf{\fa{خاکستر}}.) A storm? (\textbf{\fa{طوفان}}.) To drown? (\textbf{\fa{غرق} \fa{شدن}}.) To crash down? (\textbf{\fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن}}.) A warning? (\textbf{\fa{هشدار}}.) To warn? (\textbf{\fa{هشدار} \fa{دادن}}.) To be destroyed? (\textbf{\fa{ویران} \fa{شدن}}.) To collapse? (\textbf{\fa{فرو} \fa{ریختن}}.) Rubble? (\textbf{\fa{آوار}}.) To evacuate? (\textbf{\fa{تخلیه} \fa{کردن}}.) To take shelter? (\textbf{\fa{پناه} \fa{بردن}}.)
